title: Not All AI Workers Believe Technology Can Kill Everyone
seoTitle: AI Workers Question Total Death Risk
subtitle: Industry leaders' professionals show skepticism about warnings that technology could end humanity
excerpt: People who have worked at leading tech companies express doubt about warnings that artificial intelligence could kill all of humanity.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The debate over the future of artificial intelligence and its possible impacts on humanity is divided within the tech sector. While there are warnings that technology could end humanity, not all AI workers believe the technology could kill everyone. This stance shows that consensus on existential risks is not unanimous among those directly involved in developing these tools.

Skepticism among industry professionals

In text exchanges and conversations, several people who have worked for leading companies demonstrate skepticism toward these warnings. These professionals, with direct experience in advanced system development environments, question the most pessimistic predictions about humanity’s demise caused by technology.

The context of technology warnings

Artificial intelligence involves developing computing systems capable of performing complex tasks, such as data processing and decision making. With the advancement of these technologies, general discussions arise about their limits and safe use. Warnings about potential catastrophic dangers suggest extreme scenarios for society’s future. However, perceptions of these risks vary significantly among sector professionals.

Technological skepticism is common when it comes to predictions about the future of new systems. Workers and former employees of leading companies frequently debate the technical feasibility and practical reality of the tools they develop. In everyday conversations and text communications, these professionals assess the gap between the real capabilities of current systems and the hypothetical destruction scenarios presented in public warnings.

Thus, internal discussions among former employees of leading companies reveal that catastrophic visions are not shared by everyone. The presence of skeptics regarding severe warnings highlights the complexity of the debate on AI safety, where direct technical experience serves as a basis to challenge predictions that technology could extinguish human life.

With information from BBC News.
